sections.heading: Compare How Dummies Move After an Impact
sections.intro: In Hyper Realistic Ragdoll, each body part responds independently to punches, shots, and blasts. Limping and crawling are distinct outcomes: a dummy can limp after a shot to the leg, while a broken leg can leave it crawling. When comparing weapons, watch how the dummy gets around after the initial reaction, not just what happens at the moment of impact.
paragraphs: Use the comparison to decide what to try next, not to rank weapons or estimate damage. If one dummy limps and another crawls but they started in different conditions, repeat the comparison with similar starting conditions before attributing the difference to the weapon. Even then, describe what happened in those attempts rather than treating either reaction as guaranteed.
bullets: Note the starting condition. Before each attempt, record whether the dummy is standing or already moving and whether it is already limping or crawling.
Change one thing at a time. If you want to compare two weapons, swap the weapon while keeping the dummy's starting condition and the rest of the setup as similar as possible.
Record the reaction in two parts. Note what the dummy does on impact, then describe how it moves afterward. For example, write "stumbled on impact, then walked with a limp" rather than just "limped."

sections.heading: Use Body Scan to Inspect Broken Bones
sections.intro: Body Scan adds an X-ray view for checking broken bones. Keep that result separate from what you observe on the outside: a dummy’s movement shows its visible reaction, while the scan lets you look for a fracture. One observation alone does not establish the other.
paragraphs: For a useful comparison, watch and note the dummy’s movement first. Then use Body Scan to check for a visible broken bone, and record the scan result separately. This makes it easier to distinguish an observed movement change from an injury shown by the X-ray, without treating one as proof of the other.

For more detail about the feature, see the Body Scan guide when it is available. The game description does not specify an input for opening the scan, so check the controls shown in your session rather than assuming a key or button.

sections.heading: Use a Medkit or Defibrillator to Revive a Dummy
sections.intro: The Medkit and Defibrillator are revival tools in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll. If a dummy needs reviving during a weapon comparison, finish writing down what happened in the first trial, then use whichever revival tool you have available.
paragraphs: Before starting the second trial, check whether the revived dummy moves the same way it did at the start of the first one. For example, if it walked normally before the first trial but limps before the second, mark that difference in your notes. For a closer comparison, start the second trial with a dummy whose visible condition matches the first trial's starting condition.

faq.question: How do you unlock weapons in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll?
faq.answer: New weapons become available through play, but the Roblox description does not say what each one requires. If an item appears with a lock but no explanation, that tells you it is unavailable to equip at that moment, not which action will unlock it or how close you are.

faq.question: Where can you find the weapons list in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll?
faq.answer: Look in the Weapons and Tools portion of the official Roblox experience description. It names six weapons and indicates that there are others. Use it to check whether a particular name appears in the official description, not to determine everything you can equip in your current session.

faq.question: How do weapons interact with ragdoll physics?
faq.answer: The affected body part matters: a dummy's arm can hang limp after a break, while a hit to the head can make the dummy faint. Those are different in-game reactions, so seeing a dummy fall does not by itself tell you whether it fainted or was reacting to a limb injury.

sections.heading: Grab, Swing, and Release a Dummy in Your First Test
sections.intro: Pick one dummy and find an open patch of ground. Grab the dummy and release it without swinging. Watch which part touches the ground first and how the rest of the body moves after contact. This gives you a baseline for the next attempt. If the dummy is already moving when you grab it, wait for a steadier starting position before you let go.

Track its path after it leaves your grip, then look at how it lands. If you want another pass, change just one part of the motion, such as when you throw during the swing, and watch the same part of the landing again.

In Hyper Realistic Ragdoll, a dummy's body parts can react independently. Follow one arm or leg through both attempts so you can compare its movement with the torso. For a closer look at individual injuries, see the Body Scan guide.

sections.intro: Pick your first piece of equipment for the action you want to try. Use the stated condition as your next goal if the game shows one. See the Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Weapons Guide for the named weapons and tools when you're deciding what to try next.

sections.heading: Try a Breakable Object Before Watching a Disaster
sections.intro: For your second session in Hyper Realistic Ragdoll, pick one wall, tower, or tree and watch it break apart. You can make this your next goal without waiting for a particular weapon unlock. Keep the whole object in view and look for the first piece that separates. Then follow that piece long enough to see where it goes and check how much of the original object is still standing.
paragraphs: If Tornado, Tsunami, or Meteor Rain happens while you’re playing, pick one object you can see clearly and keep watching it as the event unfolds. If it breaks, compare what you see with your first test. Does it come apart all at once or in stages? Can you still tell where the first piece came from? Starting with a single object gives you a reference for those details, which are easy to lose when several things break at the same time.

Locked without a clear requirement: A lock tells you the Bat isn’t selectable right now, not what will make it available. Treat a lock icon without text and a message that doesn’t name a clear task the same way: stop there rather than guessing which activity to repeat. If you followed a clear instruction but the displayed progress didn’t change, reread the wording before spending time on another attempt.
Already selectable: Skip the unlock check. Select the Bat and continue to the next section to see how to use any prompt the game displays.

sections.heading: Use the Bat's On-Screen Prompt If You Can Equip It
sections.intro: Select the Bat entry if it’s available. If the game shows a separate equip prompt, use it first. Once the item is equipped, look for an action prompt on the device you’re playing on. Use the input shown there, since a prompt from another player’s clip may be for a different device.
paragraphs: Hyper Realistic Ragdoll simulates each dummy’s body parts independently, so the part affected can change how the dummy moves. If you get an action prompt, try it once on a single in-game dummy. Watch for contact, then check whether the dummy’s posture or movement changes. If it stumbles and gets back up, for example, that’s the result of that attempt. If you see the item move but miss the dummy, you’ve seen the input trigger an action and can leave the dummy’s response for another attempt.
If no action prompt appears after equipping the Bat, see the Hyper Realistic Ragdoll Controls Guide for general equipment inputs. The Bat’s specific input remains unclear without an on-screen prompt.

faq.question: Does the order of weapons in the Roblox description reveal the bat's unlock order?
faq.answer: The description presents the Katana, Sniper, and other named weapons as examples of available equipment. It gives no progression sequence connecting those weapons to a bat. If Bat appears in your session, use any prerequisite displayed on that entry to decide what to work on.

faq.question: Can Body Scan show what happened after using the bat?
faq.answer: Body Scan provides an X-ray view of broken bones in an in-game dummy. If you can equip the bat and want to check for a fracture, inspect the same dummy before and after the interaction. The scan shows bone condition, while the comparison tells you whether it changed during that attempt.

faq.question: Can an in-game dummy get back up after falling?
faq.answer: Dummies can recover and get back up on their own. If one falls while you are trying an equipped item, watch it for a moment so you can describe both the initial reaction and what follows. A Medkit and a Defibrillator are also available to bring dummies back.
